title: Review: post-KITH-hwly audit (outbox, receipt success, schema V6)
notes:
Maintainer risk: LOW — No new auth surface, no wire format changes. The P0/P1 claims from the outbox agent were false positives: the at-least-once delivery semantic with peer-side idempotency is the correct design. Real findings are: one P1 test coverage gap (receipt state machine forward path), two P2 doc/const issues, one P3 comment gap.
Confidence: 8% chance of missed bug. Uncertainty driven by: the outbox retry loop is large and was traced carefully this cycle — I am now more confident in it. The main remaining uncertainty is whether any JMAP owner-side method has an unvalidated reference to a nonexistent chat or contact that could produce unexpected behavior. Would raise confidence if: the owner-side Message/set create path for group chats with mixed-status members (some delivered, some failed) was traced end-to-end.
